subject: ss-gastroenterology
title: Diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy: techniques, classifications and safety

steps.tx: The **Boston Bowel Preparation Scale** (BBPS) provides an objective, standardized assessment of mucosal visualization across 3 distinct colonic segments: the right colon, transverse colon, and left colon. Each segment receives a score from 0 to 3 after washing and suctioning. A total composite score >= 6 with no individual segment < 2 defines **adequate preparation**, permitting reliable polyp detection and standard surveillance intervals.
steps.say: The Boston Bowel Preparation Scale provides an objective assessment of mucosal cleanliness across three colonic segments: the right colon, transverse colon, and left colon. Each segment is scored from zero to three after washing and suctioning. A composite score of at least six with no segment below two indicates adequate preparation for reliable polyp detection.

rows: Portions of mucosa seen, but other areas stained
Minor residual staining, but mucosa well seen
Entire mucosal surface cleanly seen without residue

steps.tx: **Endoscopic mucosal resection** (EMR) is designed for non-invasive superficial mucosal neoplasms. The technique utilizes **submucosal injection** of saline or viscous lifting solutions with dilute adrenaline to elevate the lesion above the muscularis propria. Creating this temporary submucosal fluid cushion separates mucosal neoplasia from muscular layers, facilitating safe electrosurgical snare excision while minimizing thermal transmural injury and perforation.
steps.say: Endoscopic mucosal resection provides safe excision for superficial mucosal neoplasms. The technique uses submucosal injection of fluid cushions to elevate mucosal lesions above the deeper muscularis propria. This fluid separation isolates the lesion, allowing complete snare excision while protecting the muscular wall from thermal perforation.

nodes.label: Submucosal injection to create fluid cushion
Elevation of mucosal lesion above muscularis

steps.tx: **Endoscopic submucosal dissection** (ESD) employs specialized electrosurgical knives to dissect directly through the submucosal layer beneath a target lesion. ESD is indicated for large (> 20 mm) or fibrotic mucosal neoplasms. Unlike piecemeal snare resection, ESD achieves complete **en bloc resection** regardless of specimen size, guaranteeing precise histological assessment of lateral and deep margins and lowering local recurrence rates.
steps.say: Endoscopic submucosal dissection uses specialized electrosurgical knives to dissect through the submucosa beneath a target lesion. It is indicated for large or fibrotic neoplasms exceeding twenty millimetres. Endoscopic submucosal dissection achieves complete en bloc resection regardless of lesion size, ensuring accurate histological staging.

left.title: Endoscopic Mucosal Resection (EMR)
points: Higher recurrence rate for large lesions

right.title: Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection (ESD)
points: En bloc curative resection regardless of size
Clear lateral and deep margin assessment

steps.tx: Therapeutic **ERCP complications** require prompt recognition and structured management. Overall incidence of acute pancreatitis ranges from 3% to 10%, mitigated by routine rectal NSAID suppositories and pancreatic duct stenting. Duodenal perforation follows the **Stapfer classification**: Type I involves free lateral duodenal wall tears, Type II involves retroperitoneal peri-ampullary tears, Type III involves ductal tears, and Type IV involves retroperitoneal air alone.
steps.say: Major complications of ERCP require vigilant recognition and management. Acute pancreatitis occurs in three to ten percent of procedures, mitigated by prophylactic rectal anti-inflammatory suppositories. Duodenal perforations are categorized by the Stapfer classification into Types 1 to 4, determining whether surgical repair or conservative management is indicated.

rows: Lateral or medial duodenal wall (endoscope trauma)
Conservative: bowel rest, antibiotics, biliary stent
Distal bile or pancreatic duct injury (wires / baskets)
Endoscopic stenting to divert bile flow

steps.tx: **Fine-needle biopsy** (EUS-FNB) using advanced **Franseen needle** geometries (crown-tip with three symmetrical cutting edges) or fork-tip designs has revolutionized endosonographic tissue acquisition. Unlike standard cytology aspiration needles that yield only dissociated cells, FNB cores preserve contiguous histological tissue architecture, permitting immunohistochemistry, molecular profiling, and superior diagnostic adequacy for submucosal stromal tumours and pancreatic masses.
steps.say: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy using advanced Franseen needles has revolutionized diagnostic tissue sampling. By using three symmetrical cutting edges, Franseen needles obtain intact tissue cores rather than loose cytology aspirates. This architecture allows detailed immunohistochemistry and molecular profiling for pancreatic and stromal neoplasms.

vis.caption: The needle drawn here is labelled fine-needle aspiration of a pancreatic mass. A Franseen fine-needle biopsy uses the same echoendoscope route to take a tissue core. Illustration: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The **Kudo pit pattern** classification categorizes colorectal mucosal crypt orifices using **magnification chromoendoscopy**. Types I (round pits) and II (papillary/stellar pits) reflect non-neoplastic mucosa. Types 3 and 4 (tubular or gyrus-like pits) represent adenomatous polyps amenable to endoscopic resection. Type 5 (loss of pit architecture) indicates deep submucosal invasive adenocarcinoma, requiring surgical oncologic resection.
steps.say: The Kudo pit pattern classification assesses colorectal crypt orifices under magnification chromoendoscopy. Types one and two reflect benign non-neoplastic tissue. Types 3 and 4 indicate adenomatous polyps suitable for endoscopic resection. Type 5 exhibits disordered or absent crypt architecture indicative of deep submucosal cancer requiring surgical resection.

rows: Normal colonic mucosa; no resection needed
Small or large tubular / round pits
Tubular adenoma; resect by EMR or polypectomy
Tubulovillous adenoma; resect by EMR / ESD
Deep submucosal invasive cancer; oncologic surgery

steps.tx: The **NICE classification** (NBI International Colorectal Endoscopic) stratifies colorectal polyps using **narrow-band imaging** without optical magnification. Type 1 lesions appear light or pale with regular vessels, indicating hyperplastic polyps. Type 2 lesions exhibit brown vessels surrounding white structures, indicating adenomas suitable for endoscopic resection. Type 3 lesions display disrupted, avascular regions, signaling deep submucosal invasive carcinoma.
steps.say: The NICE classification evaluates colorectal polyps with narrow-band imaging without optical magnification. Type one lesions appear pale with faint vessels, identifying hyperplastic polyps. Type two lesions show brown vessels outlining white mucosal pits, confirming adenomas suitable for endoscopic excision. Type three lesions display avascular disorganized areas that signal deep submucosal cancer.

rows: Pale colour, faint/absent vessels, uniform dark spots
Hyperplastic polyp; leave in place or discard
Brown vessels surrounding white mucosal structures
Distorted, avascular, or missing vessels with dull surface
Deep submucosal invasive cancer; staging & oncologic surgery

steps.tx: **Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy** (PEG) provides safe, long-term **enteral nutrition access** for patients with functional gastrointestinal tracts who cannot maintain oral intake due to neurological dysphagia, head and neck cancers, or trauma. The procedure relies on direct endoscopic gastric transillumination and external 1:1 finger indentation against the anterior abdominal wall to confirm a safe gastropexy window before trocar insertion.
steps.say: Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy establishes durable enteral feeding access for patients with intact intestinal function who cannot swallow safely. Placement relies on direct endoscopic transillumination and corresponding external finger indentation against the anterior abdominal wall to confirm an unobstructed gastropexy path before inserting the feeding tube.
